sources.citation: Daniels, Don. 2016. Magɨ: An Undocumented Language of Papua New Guinea. Oceanic Linguistics 55(1): 199-224. doi:10.1353/ol.2016.0004. Open Access publisher PDF via ANU Open Research, hdl:1885/108658.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent. Section 3.1 Phonology (pp. 205-206) compares Magɨ and Aisi phoneme inventories (Magɨ retains /r/ vs /d/ contrast, has rare /ñ/, lacks /o/) and allophony of voiced stops; no statement on stress, accent, tone or prosody anywhere in the article (the only hits for 'stress'/'accent' are about language attitudes and a speaker's 'different accent').

sources.citation: Daniels, Don. 2015. A Reconstruction of Proto-Sogeram: Phonology, Lexicon, and Morphosyntax. PhD dissertation, University of California, Santa Barbara. 1127 pp. (Appendix 4 'Aisi Grammar Sketch', pp. 766-882; phonology section 4.2, pp. 771-776). eScholarship ark:/13030/qt1kj4174g.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing for Aisi/Magɨ: section 4.2 (pp. 771-776) gives consonant and vowel inventories, /k/ palatalization in Magɨ, voiced-stop lenition, glide syllabification, /ɨ/ minimal pairs, and morphophonemics (epenthesis, rounding, assimilation) with no mention of stress, accent or tone. The sketch is explicitly 'primarily a sketch of Aisi Mabɨŋ' (p. 768). The only stress remark in the entire dissertation is p. 71 (Mand sound change): 'Further research into the stress systems of the Sogeram languages might reveal a consistent pattern.'
